chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father from a man

He wrote to the Virtuous Servant (peace be upon him) asking him: I deal with a people, I sell them flour, making a profit of two dirhams per qafiz for a known period, and they ask me to give them dirhams for half a qafiz of flour. Is there a way for me so that I do not enter into the forbidden? So he wrote to him: Lend them the dirhams as a loan, and increase the price for them on half a qafiz by the amount you used to profit from them.

key_terms.الْحَرَام: The forbidden (specifically riba/usury in this context)
key_terms.الْقَفِيز: A unit of volume measurement used in trade

ai.seo_question: How to avoid usury when selling goods on credit with a price increase?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the classical Shia juristic mechanism of *hiyal* (legal stratagems) to avoid *riba al-jahiliyya* by decoupling the loan from the sale, a method notably debated by scholars like Al-Shafi'i and Al-Awza'i. It highlights the practical application of separating the principal debt from the commodity transaction to ensure the profit is derived from trade rather than interest on money. This ruling remains central to understanding how early Imams navigated commercial complexities in pre-modern markets.
